To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the quasiparticles are not diffusing, but rather the combined gas of the quasifluctuations and the phonons is diffusing.

the quasiparticles propagate ballistically at low temperatures, that the quasihole diffusion is faster than the quasiparton diffusion, that the quasicarrier recombination time is much shorter than the quasiholes, and that the quasicarrer recombination time is temperature independent.
the quasiparticles propagate ballistically in superconducting Pb at low temperature and that the quasiballistic regime persists up to temperatures of at least T = 1.3 K.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the propagation characteristics of quasicarriers (quasiparticles and Cooper pairs) in superconductors.
the propagation characteristics of quasi-particles in superconducting lead.
the propagation characteristics of quaisiparticles in bulk, superconductor single crystals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quasiparticles propagate as an ideal gas in bulk superconductors, but with a recombination time which is at least an order magnitude larger than the quasipartide lifetime.
the quasiparticles do not propagate in bulk Pb, at least at temperatures below 1 K.
the recombination of quasiparticle pairs in superconductors is not a single step process but involves a sequence of processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the quasiparticles propagate in bulk Pb in a manner similar to the propagation of excitons in a semiconductor, and that the decay time of their density is determined by the quasipartical recombination time.
we have measured the propagation of quasiparticle excitations in superconducting Pb, and that the quasiparticles recombine with a characteristic time of about 10 ns.

the propagation characteristics are dominated by quasiparticle scattering with phonons, and that the quasiparticles recombine with each other on a time scale much shorter than the time scale for the decay of the quasparticle density.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quasiparticles are not the only relevant degrees of freedom in the bulk superconductor.
the recombination of quasiparticle pairs is the dominant mechanism for quasiparticle decay, and not phonon scattering.
the recombination of quasiparticle pairs is a slow process.
